questions.stem: Which river flows through Kaziranga National Park, the UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for the Great One-Horned Rhinoceros?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga National Park in Assam lies along the southern bank of the Brahmaputra River. The park harbours approximately two-thirds of the world's Great One-Horned Rhinoceros population. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Jim Corbett National Park, established in 1936, was India's first national park. Under what name was it originally established?
questions.explanation: Jim Corbett National Park was originally established as Hailey National Park in 1936, named after Sir William Malcolm Hailey, the then-Governor of the United Provinces. It was later renamed after the famous naturalist Jim Corbett, who championed its creation. It was the first park established under Project Tiger in 1973.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Keoladeo Ghana National Park (Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary), a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for migratory birds, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Keoladeo Ghana National Park is located near Bharatpur in Rajasthan. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985. The park is a wintering ground for enormous numbers of Siberian cranes and other migratory waterfowl. It was formerly a duck-hunting reserve of the Maharajas of Bharatpur.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Which was the first Biosphere Reserve established in India?
questions.explanation: The Nilgiris Biosphere Reserve, established in 1986, was the first biosphere reserve in India under the UNESCO Man and Biosphere (MAB) programme. It spans Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka and includes Mudumalai, Bandipur, Nagarhole, Wayanad, Mukurthi, and Silent Valley. As of 2024, India has 18 biosphere reserves.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Project Elephant, launched by the Government of India to protect elephants and their corridors, was initiated in which year?
questions.explanation: Project Elephant was launched in 1992 by the Ministry of Environment and Forests to protect elephants, their habitats, and migration corridors. It provides financial and technical support to major elephant-bearing states. India has the world's largest population of Asian elephants. Project Tiger, by comparison, was launched in 1973.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Periyar Tiger Reserve, known for its large populations of elephants and tigers, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Periyar National Park and Tiger Reserve is located in the Cardamom and Pandalam Hills of Idukki and Pathanamthitta districts in Kerala. The Periyar Lake at its centre was created by the Mullaperiyar Dam. It is one of the most visited wildlife reserves in India.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Manas National Park in Assam, a UNESCO World Heritage Site declared in 1985, is a transboundary conservation area shared with which country?
questions.explanation: Manas National Park adjoins the Royal Manas National Park in Bhutan, forming a transboundary conservation complex along the foothills of the Himalayas. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, a Project Tiger reserve, and a biosphere reserve. It is home to the Assam Roofed Turtle, Golden Langur, and the rare Pygmy Hog.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: The Valley of Flowers National Park and Nanda Devi National Park together form a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Both are located in which state?
questions.explanation: Both Valley of Flowers National Park and Nanda Devi National Park are located in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand. Together they form the Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve and jointly received UNESCO World Heritage Site status. Valley of Flowers is renowned for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers. Nanda Devi (7,816 m) is the highest peak entirely within India.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: The Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary (Little Rann of Kutch), home to the last wild population of Indian Wild Ass (Khur), is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The Wild Ass Wildlife Sanctuary in the Little Rann of Kutch is located in the Surendra Nagar and Patan districts of Gujarat. The Indian Wild Ass (Equus hemionus khur, locally called Khur) is found only in this region. The Little Rann of Kutch is a seasonal saltmarsh that floods during monsoon.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Sariska Tiger Reserve, which made headlines in 2004–05 when its entire tiger population was found poached, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Sariska Tiger Reserve is located in the Alwar district of Rajasthan. After poaching wiped out its tiger population around 2004, tigers were translocated from Ranthambore (the first-ever inter-reserve tiger translocation in India) beginning in 2008, restoring the population. It is the only reserve to have successfully relocated tigers in India.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Dachigam National Park, located near Srinagar, is specifically established to protect which critically endangered species?
questions.explanation: Dachigam National Park (near Srinagar, J&K) is the primary protected habitat for the Hangul (Cervus hanglu hanglu), also called the Kashmir Stag. It is the only surviving subspecies of the Central European Red Deer in the Indian subcontinent. The Hangul is the state animal of J&K and is critically endangered with a very small population.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Which national park is the largest in India by area and also holds one of the world's highest densities of snow leopards?
questions.explanation: Hemis National Park in Ladakh, covering approximately 3,350 sq km, is the largest national park in India. It lies entirely above 3,000 m altitude in the Trans-Himalayan region and is one of the few places in the world where snow leopards can be observed with reasonable regularity. Namdapha (Arunachal) at ~1,985 sq km is the second largest.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Ranthambore National Park, one of India's most famous tiger reserves, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Ranthambore National Park is located in the Sawai Madhopur district of Rajasthan. It is one of the largest and most renowned wildlife reserves in northern India, known especially for its Bengal tiger sightings. The park includes the ruins of Ranthambore Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Kanha National Park in Madhya Pradesh is historically famous as the inspiration for which classic piece of literature?
options: B) The Jungle Book by Rudyard Kipling
C) Wild Animals I Have Known by Ernest Thompson Seton
D) Born Free by Joy Adamson
questions.explanation: Kanha National Park, with its sal forests and open meadows (maidans), is widely credited as the inspiration for Rudyard Kipling's 'The Jungle Book' (1894). Kipling's characters Mowgli, Shere Khan, and Baloo are set in forests closely resembling Kanha. Kanha is also where the rare barasingha (swamp deer) was saved from extinction.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Eravikulam National Park in Kerala, situated in the Anamalai Hills, is primarily established to protect which endangered mountain ungulate?
questions.explanation: Eravikulam National Park near Munnar in Kerala was established in 1978 specifically to protect the Nilgiri Tahr (Nilgiritragus hylocrius), a mountain goat endemic to the Western Ghats. The park's Rajamala area has the world's highest concentration of this species. Anaimudi (2,695 m), the highest peak in peninsular India, lies within the park.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Bandhavgarh National Park, which has one of the highest densities of Bengal tigers in India, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Bandhavgarh National Park is located in the Umaria and Katni districts of Madhya Pradesh. It was originally the hunting reserve of the Maharajas of Rewa and was declared a national park in 1968. It has one of the highest densities of Bengal tigers in India. The historic Bandhavgarh Fort, believed to be at least 2,000 years old, stands within the park.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: The Sundarbans National Park, the world's largest mangrove forest and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is shared between India and which other country?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans spans the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta across India (West Bengal) and Bangladesh. The Indian portion is the Sundarbans National Park, a UNESCO WHS since 1987. The Bangladeshi portion is the Sundarbans Reserve Forest, also a UNESCO WHS. The forest is the natural habitat of the Bengal Tiger and the Irrawaddy Dolphin.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: India's commitments under CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species) are administered by which ministry?
options: A) Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
B) Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
D) Ministry of Science and Technology
questions.explanation: India is a signatory to CITES (signed 1973, entered into force 1975), and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) is the designated CITES Management Authority in India. The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) under MoEFCC enforces CITES provisions. CITES regulates international trade in over 38,000 species of animals and plants.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Silent Valley National Park, known for its undisturbed tropical rainforest and the campaign that blocked a hydroelectric project in the 1970s–80s, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Silent Valley National Park is located in the Nilgiri Hills of Palakkad district, Kerala. A proposed Kunthipuzha River dam threatened the valley in the 1970s; massive public opposition led by the Kerala Sastra Sahitya Parishad and supported by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi resulted in the project's cancellation and the valley's protection as a national park in 1984.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Nokrek Biosphere Reserve in Meghalaya, recognized under UNESCO's Man and Biosphere Programme, is notable primarily as a gene sanctuary for which plant?
questions.explanation: Nokrek Biosphere Reserve is home to Citrus indica, also known as the 'Indian wild orange,' which is the wild ancestor of all citrus fruits. It is therefore classified as a gene sanctuary for wild citrus species. Nokrek is in the West Garo Hills of Meghalaya and was designated a UNESCO MAB Biosphere Reserve in 2009. The reserve is also the habitat of the Red Panda.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Project Tiger was launched in India in which year, with Jim Corbett National Park as one of the first nine reserves?
questions.explanation: Project Tiger was launched on 1 April 1973 under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, with nine initial tiger reserves. The tiger census of 1972 had revealed a dramatic decline to around 1,827 tigers. As of 2023, India has 53 tiger reserves and approximately 3,682 tigers — about 75% of the world's wild tiger population.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: India's first marine national park, established in 1982, is located in the Gulf of Kutch in which state?
questions.explanation: The Marine National Park in the Gulf of Kutch (Jamnagar, Gujarat), notified as a sanctuary in 1980 and as a national park in 1982, was India's first marine national park. It protects coral reefs, sea turtles, dolphins, and sea snakes. The Gulf of Mannar in Tamil Nadu is a separate marine biosphere reserve declared in 1989.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Gir National Park, the world's only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the Junagadh and Gir Somnath districts of Gujarat. It is the last refuge of the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica). The lion population has recovered from around 20 in the 1890s to over 600 today. The Maldharis, a pastoral community, coexist with the lions in the forest.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, the primary legislation governing wildlife conservation and trade in India, was enacted in which year?
questions.explanation: The Wildlife (Protection) Act was enacted in 1972, the same year the Stockholm Conference on Human Environment was held. The Act created a framework for protected areas (national parks, sanctuaries, conservation reserves, community reserves) and schedules of protected species. It was significantly amended in 2002 and 2022. The 2022 amendment aligns India's law with CITES.
questions.subject: environment

questions.stem: Bhitarkanika National Park in Odisha is among India's most important protected areas primarily because of its large population of which species?
questions.explanation: Bhitarkanika National Park in Kendrapara district, Odisha, harbours one of India's largest populations of Saltwater Crocodiles (Crocodylus porosus), the world's largest living reptile. The adjacent Gahirmatha Marine Sanctuary is a nesting site for Olive Ridley Sea Turtles (Lepidochelys olivacea), home to one of the world's largest mass nesting events (Arribada). Bhitarkanika is a Ramsar Wetland.
questions.subject: environment
